component.name: DrukhalManager
component.summary: Manage Stellaris mods and merge their conflicts

description.p: A native Linux mod manager for Stellaris that edits your load order, finds where mods conflict, and merges them into a patch so every mod's changes survive.
A fork of Irony Mod Manager by Mario (bcssov), rewritten in Rust with GTK and libadwaita.

ul.li: Edit the load order and keep several collections, synced to the Paradox Launcher
Find files and objects that several mods change
Merge conflicts with AI, or pick a version, into a patch mod
Repair files with brace mistakes and broken mod descriptors
See which mods caused the errors the game logged

description.p: Notifications in one place. A bell in the header keeps every notification, newest first, with its time and its button, such as Show or Restart. Dismiss them one by one, or all at once with Clear All. Repeats are folded into one, and a badge counts the new ones. Toasts no longer stay on screen until closed.

Notes on mods. Write yourself a note on any mod, such as why it sits where it does, from its menu. The note shows as an icon on the row and in the mod's details, where you can edit it in place. Search finds notes, and a shared collection file can carry them.

Diagnostics for bug reports. DrukhalManager now keeps a small log of scans, merged patch changes, AI calls, game sessions and update checks. It never holds API keys, prompts or file contents. Main Menu, then Troubleshooting, copies a report to paste into a bug report or opens the log folder.

Categories in the Load Order. The sidebar lists the Smart Sort categories with how many mods each holds; click one to see only its mods. The load order shows a small header wherever the category changes, and says when mods were moved there by hand. Turn the headers off in the Smart Sort menu.
Faster conflict scans. Scans remember what they read, so a rescan only reads the files that changed, even after restarting the app.
Fixes. The Conflicts page no longer freezes for a few seconds after a scan or while searching.
Changed Lines Only. A new toggle on the Conflicts page folds the lines that are the same in both versions, keeping a few around each difference. Click a fold to open it.
Put This In. Right-click a difference on the view-only version to copy those lines into the version you're editing.

Keyboard shortcuts for conflicts. Alt+Page Down and Alt+Page Up move between conflicts, Alt+Left and Alt+Right use the left or right version, Alt+M merges with AI and Alt+I ignores a conflict. They're listed in Keyboard Shortcuts.
Choose the Claude model. Preferences → AI Merging lets you pick which Claude model merges, with its price, and cost estimates follow your choice.
Fixes. Preferences now says whether your API keys are in the system keyring or, when there is none, in DrukhalManager's own settings file. A Steam Web API key can be saved without a keyring.

One merged patch per collection. Merges only fit the load order they were made for, so each collection now has its own merged patch, named after it, and switching collections switches patches. The patch you had becomes the active collection's. Backups, exporting with the patch and importing work per collection: an imported patch goes to the new collection instead of replacing yours.

Freeze a collection. Freeze This Collection…, in the collection menu, copies its Workshop mods into local mods, so Steam updating one can't break a campaign in progress. The health strip shows when Steam has newer versions, and Unfreeze switches back to the Workshop mods and deletes the copies.
Merge Tool… for whole files. Overridden text files on the Conflicts page, and the file merge dialog, can be merged in Meld, KDiff3, VS Code or another tool too.

Multiplayer check. The report says whether you run the native Linux build or the Windows one, as players report that their checksums never match. Comparing reports now points out files that differ only in line endings, and files the native Linux build may skip because of how their names are capitalised.
Smoother Preferences. Preferences is split into Game, Merging, AI Merging, Steam and Updates pages, and opens without stuttering. The Conflicts page fits narrower windows.

A redesigned load order. A health strip above the list shows what needs attention: mods not updated for the game, required mods that are missing, mods loading before ones they need, out-of-date merges and achievements, each with a button to show or fix it. A sidebar of views lists the mods that need attention, aren't updated, have conflicts, turn off achievements or are disabled. Rows take one line each, and selecting a mod shows its problems, needs and actions in a panel beside the list.

Workshop required items. With your own Steam Web API key, set in Preferences, mods' Workshop “Required items” are checked like dependencies: missing, disabled or late ones are pointed out, sorting puts them first, and Get Required Mods enables or opens them. Items that aren't really mods, such as “Stellaris 101: How to Read”, are left out, and any other can be dismissed.
Mods not updated yet. After a game update, DrukhalManager lists the enabled mods that don't support the new version yet, and can set them aside in a collection until they do.

Campaigns remember their mods. Each campaign remembers the mods it was played with. Launching it with different mods asks first, and offers to switch back to its collection. Saves… lists campaigns and their mods.
Find the Crashing Mod… narrows down the mod that crashes the game by halving the enabled mods between launches, keeping dependencies together, and puts your load order back at the end.
Fixes. Messages no longer go blank when a name contains “&”, and long ones wrap.
Merge into One Mod can write the merged mod as one zip file, and can write it to an extra mod folder.
An Extra Mod Folder, in Preferences, lists and loads the mods kept in it, such as local mods on another drive or in a git checkout.
Export with the Merged Patch saves a collection together with its merged patch in one zip. Importing it installs the patch, after backing up yours.
The multiplayer report can include all the game's files, to find modified or damaged ones outside the multiplayer checksum. Repeated reports are faster, as file hashes are remembered.

Merge Tool… on the Conflicts page opens two versions of a definition in Meld, KDiff3, VS Code or another tool set in Preferences, and uses what you save. The Flatpak needs a one-time permission for it, which the app explains.

The mod search understands filters: enabled:, source:, achievements:, conflicts: and version:, with -- to leave mods out, || for either, and quoted phrases. It also finds mods by Workshop ID. The Filters button next to the search box sets them for you.

Collections can be imported from the game's current load order and from Paradox Launcher playset files, and exported as a playset file for players who use the launcher. Import and export are now submenus of the collection menu.
The name Merge into One Mod gives the merged mod can be chosen in Preferences, with {Name} for the collection's name.
Overridden images, including DDS textures, are shown side by side on the Conflicts page with their sizes, and Use This Version puts the chosen copy in the merged patch.

Copy Load Order and Paste Load Order, in the collection menu, share a load order as a numbered list with Workshop links, ready for a chat or forum post. Pasting one, or a collection file, makes a new collection.
Mods can be renamed with names only DrukhalManager shows, such as "UIOD" for a long Workshop title. Search finds both names.
A collection keeps the mods it lists that aren't installed, under Not Installed, with a Workshop link. When one is installed and the mods are reloaded, it goes back into its place.
DLC… in the main menu turns DLCs on and off.
The Disabled list can be sorted by name or by when mods were last updated.
Include Test Versions, in Preferences, offers betas and release candidates as well.

Smart Sort arranges the load order the way the Stellaris community's guides suggest: unofficial patches first, then graphics, flavor, shipsets, galaxy generation, gameplay and large overhauls, compatibility patches, UI mods and their patches, and universal patches last. Sub-mods go directly below the mod they need, and every mod still loads after its dependencies. A preview shows where each mod goes and why, and any mod can be moved to another section; the choice is remembered.
Sort A–Z, Dependencies First sorts the load order by name while keeping mods after their dependencies.
Merge All now works on folders of overridden files too, with one AI call per object the copies disagree on.
Text boxes, such as the AI's reasoning, merged results and the file editors, can be resized by dragging the grip below them.

After a Stellaris update, merges are checked against the new game too: ones whose objects or files the base game has added since are flagged as outdated, base-game definitions that moved to another file are followed instead of reported missing, and the reasons name the update.

The merged patch is backed up before each Merge All and before merges are removed. Merged Patch Backups in the main menu restores any of the last ten, so a batch merge that went wrong can be undone in one step.
The Flatpak now applies custom libadwaita colour schemes from ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css, such as DankMaterialShell's or matugen's, and picks up a new palette while it's open.
When an update needs a new Flatpak permission, which the app can't install itself, it says how to update instead.

Choose which localisation languages the conflict scan reads, in Preferences under Game. It defaults to the game's language, so translations you don't play in no longer show up as conflicts, and localisation can be left out of the scan altogether.
The Flatpak applies custom libadwaita colour schemes from your GTK 4 stylesheet.

Conflicts between a mod and the mods it depends on, such as a compatibility patch and the mods it patches, are hidden, since the patch is meant to override them. Show them again from Rules… on the Conflicts page.
When an AI merge comes back broken, the error goes back to the model once for a corrected version before the merge counts as failed.
Merge All can merge several objects at once; set how many in Preferences. Merges wait and try again when the provider is rate limited.

Ignore rules: hide conflicts by path, such as gfx/** or localisation/*, optionally only for an exact set of mods. Open them with Rules… on the Conflicts page, which previews how many conflicts each rule hides.
The mod list marks Workshop mods with an update Steam hasn't finished downloading, mods still downloading, and mods you unsubscribed from.
The Conflicts page shows which mod's version the game uses today, and why: file names, the folder's rule, or the load order.
Fixed merges in some folders, such as scripted variables and component templates, being ignored by the game. Merges already saved there are moved to the right place.
The Conflicts page has a new look: conflicts are listed in a sidebar, and each one shows the two versions side by side with the differences highlighted.
The later-loading version can be edited by hand before you use it, and your edits can be undone.

More mod thumbnails show up: mods without a picture in their descriptor use their thumbnail.png, file names match whatever their capitalisation, and Workshop mods with no image on disk show their Workshop preview.
The merged patch is marked with the app's icon.
Fixed the conflict scan failing when a mod has files with non-English characters in their names.
A failed scan now shows what went wrong.

Conflicts that need no AI, because only one mod changed the object from the base game or every mod ships the same version, are marked on the Conflicts page. Merge All saves them directly, without calls or cost, and the merge dialog fills in the version to use.
Workshop mods have new menu items: Open in Steam, Open Workshop Page in Browser, Copy Workshop Link and Unsubscribe in Steam.
Looking up the base game's versions of many objects is much faster.

Merge All merges every conflicting object in a folder with AI. It shows the number of calls and an estimated cost first, streams the model's thinking under each object, lets you view each merged result, and reports the tokens and cost actually used.
Workshop mods downloaded by Steam now appear without starting the Paradox Launcher, and updated mods show their new name and version.
Reload Mods (F5 or Ctrl+R) picks up mods subscribed, updated or removed while the app is open, keeping the load order.
Steam Workshop collections can be imported as a collection, with links to subscribe to any mods that are missing.
A whole collection can be merged into one mod.
Localisation files that hold several languages can now be merged.
Interface (.gui) and graphics (.gfx) files can now be merged object by object, as can files that repeat one kind of object, such as ambient objects or font overrides.
The Conflicts page can be filtered to one mod, and Show Conflicts in a mod's menu opens it filtered.
Inline scripts are no longer reported as conflicting objects.
Mods that turn off achievements are marked in the load order, and the status line says whether your collection keeps them.
The Launch button's menu can continue your last save directly.
Mods show their thumbnails in the load order.
New Multiplayer Check in the main menu: save a report of your game and mods to send to the other players, or open theirs to see which mods, files, versions or load order differ.
API keys are now kept in your system keyring instead of the settings file; a key saved earlier moves there the next time you start DrukhalManager.
Press ? or Ctrl+? (or use the main menu) to see the keyboard shortcuts.
Zipped mods are now scanned for conflicts and can be merged like any other mod.
Merges saved by versions before 0.1.0 are listed on the Conflicts page so you can check them; keeping one makes DrukhalManager notice when its mods change.
Installing an update from inside the Flatpak works; before, clicking Update did nothing. On desktops where Flatpak can't ask whether the app may update itself, DrukhalManager now says so.
The Flatpak now points out errors Stellaris logged about your mods after you play, as the native build does, and both say when the game crashed.
Preferences explain why the game executable can't be changed in the Flatpak.
Preferences now cover the game: choose the executable and data directory, add launch options, refresh mod descriptors before playing, and close after launching.
DrukhalManager shows its version in About and Preferences, tells you when a new version is out, and in the Flatpak installs it and restarts into it.
Undo and redo for the load order (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z). The Flatpak now updates itself through its own signed repository.
First release: load order editing and collections, conflict detection, AI-assisted merging into a patch mod, file repair, load order checks and game error reports.
